question.text: A liquid fund that primarily invests in treasury bills and overnight securities would most likely have which Risk-o-meter category?

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI Risk-o-meter assigns each scheme a category determined by prescribed quantitative parameters covering credit, interest-rate and liquidity risk. A liquid fund that primarily invests in treasury bills and overnight securities carries minimal credit risk and very low interest-rate risk because of the short residual maturity of the instruments, and is conventionally placed near the lower end of the Risk-o-meter scale — within "Low to Moderate" rather than the higher categories. The Trap: "Very High", "Moderately High" and "High" are inappropriate categories for treasury-bill / overnight portfolios because such instruments do not carry the credit and duration risk that those categories assume. Note: The cited NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors Certification Examination Workbook (November 2025, pages 108, 282, 284 and 290) lists the six Risk-o-meter levels and states that each scheme determines its risk from prescribed parameters, but does not explicitly assign liquid funds or treasury-bill/overnight portfolios to the "Low to Moderate" category — if anything, the source language describes liquid funds as lowest-risk, highly liquid and negligibly volatile. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of Risk-o-meter categorisation.
